summary: Reconcile the validated S24 Android phantom-process headroom so claw-live and other Termux children are not trimmed again after DeviceConfig drift.
reason: The documented 128 override disappeared while the S24 stayed up; ActivityManager returned to effective 32 and live logs again showed Termux PhantomProcessRecord kills with reason Trimming phantom processes.

tests.name: phantom-headroom-unit
tests.evidence: 3/3 deterministic fake-ADB cases passed: healthy read-only, 32->128 verified repair, failed repair using existing backoff.

tests.name: health-and-supervision-regression
tests.evidence: Incident runtime hardening PASS; supervisor lock 1/1; health verdict 12/12.

tests.name: tier0-clawlive-rdc-slack-regression
tests.evidence: Tier0 13/13, Claw Live 22/22, RDC watchdog 16/16, capability recovery PASS, Slack runtime contract 6/6.

capabilities.reason: Restores an already documented runtime invariant for the existing Claw Live/Termux execution plane; no capability interface, authorization, MCP tool or routing contract changes.

mcp_owner_parity.reason: The repair changes only Android phantom-process headroom reconciliation inside the existing Health Manager. No MCP schema, adapter, authorization, capability graph, route, receipt, status or artifact behavior changes.

architecture.reason: Reuses the existing Health Manager, canonical ADB check and existing backoff/incident path; no new daemon, scheduler, store, router or recovery owner.

rollback: Promote the previous verified immutable Tier0 release and revert this scoped commit after checking concurrent work. DeviceConfig deletion returns Android to OEM default 32 but reintroduces the proven trimming risk.
limitations: The exact actor that removed the prior DeviceConfig override is not proven; no attribution is made.

live_acceptance.background_return: claw-live PID 19617 survived 120s background interval and return to Termux
